title: Creation and Providence
summary: God made all things out of nothing, and He upholds and governs all He has made.
description: This course studies what the Bible teaches about God as Creator and Sustainer. It covers creation out of nothing, the goodness and purpose of creation, how Christians understand Genesis 1 alongside science, God's ongoing providence over nature, nations and individuals, and how this shapes worship, work and trust in hard times.
objectives: Teach that God created all things out of nothing by His word
Explain the goodness, order and purpose of creation
Present fairly the main Christian views on the days of Genesis
Explain God's providence: preserving, governing and caring
outcomes: Explain creation ex nihilo from Scripture
Show the involvement of Father, Son and Spirit in creation
Describe the young-earth, old-earth and framework views fairly
Define providence and its three aspects
Apply providence to suffering, prayer and daily work

modules.title: In the Beginning God Created
modules.intro: This week we see that God alone is eternal and that everything else exists because He made it.

lessons.title: Out of nothing, by His word
lessons.body:
"In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth" (Genesis 1:1). Before creation there was only God. He did not shape something already there; He made all things **out of nothing** (Latin: *ex nihilo*). "The worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear" (Hebrews 11:3).

God created by speaking: "And God said, Let there be light: and there was light" (Genesis 1:3). "He spake, and it was done" (Psalm 33:9).

This means God depends on nothing, while everything depends on Him.

lessons.title: The triune Creator
lessons.body:
All three Persons of the Trinity were active in creation. The Father planned (1 Corinthians 8:6). The Son is the Word through whom "all things were made" (John 1:3); "by him were all things created... all things were created by him, and for him" (Colossians 1:16). The Spirit "moved upon the face of the waters" (Genesis 1:2) and gives life (Psalm 104:30).

Creation is not divine. God is distinct from His world, unlike in pantheism, which says everything is God. Yet He is near to it and active within it.

lessons.title: Why did God create?
lessons.body:
God did not create because He was lonely or lacking. The Father, Son and Spirit enjoyed perfect fellowship from eternity (John 17:24).

He created for His own glory: "Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created" (Revelation 4:11). Creation displays His power, wisdom and goodness (Psalm 104:24).

We were made to know, enjoy and glorify Him. Isaiah speaks of people "whom I have created for my glory" (Isaiah 43:7).

terms.def: God's making of all things out of nothing.
God as the maker of everything that exists besides Himself.
The false belief that everything is God.
The belief that God made the world but does not act in it.
A command; God created by His spoken word.
The display of God's perfections, the purpose of creation.

texts.teaches: God created the heaven and the earth in the beginning.
The worlds were framed by God's word, not from visible things.
All things were created by Christ and for Him.
God is worthy of glory because He created all things.
God created His people for His glory.

summary: God alone is eternal; He created everything else out of nothing.
Father, Son and Spirit all worked in creation.
God created for His glory, and we were made to glorify Him.

questions.q: What does creation ex nihilo mean?
Through whom were all things made, according to John 1:3?
Which belief says God made the world but no longer acts in it?

modules.title: Very Good: The Shape of Creation
modules.intro: God called His creation very good. This week we look at its order, the six days and the Sabbath rest.

lessons.title: Six days of ordered work
lessons.body:
Genesis 1 shows God bringing order and fulness. In the first three days He forms realms: light and darkness, sky and sea, land and plants. In the next three He fills them: sun, moon and stars; birds and fish; animals and man.

Repeatedly "God saw that it was good", and at the end, "behold, it was very good" (Genesis 1:31). Matter, the body and the physical world are not evil, as some ancient religions taught. They are God's good gifts (1 Timothy 4:4).

The creation reflects a wise, purposeful Maker, not blind chance.

lessons.title: Rest and the Sabbath
lessons.body:
"On the seventh day God ended his work... and he rested" (Genesis 2:2). God was not tired; He rested in the sense of finishing and delighting in His work.

God blessed the seventh day and later gave the Sabbath to Israel as a sign, patterned on creation (Exodus 20:8-11). Jesus said, "The sabbath was made for man" (Mark 2:27).

The pattern of work and rest remains a gift. Hebrews also speaks of a deeper rest believers enter by faith in Christ (Hebrews 4:9-10). Christians gather especially on the Lord's Day, the first day of the week, the day of resurrection (Acts 20:7).

lessons.title: How Christians read the days
lessons.body:
Bible-believing Christians agree that God created all things, that Adam and Eve were real, and that Genesis is true. They differ on how to read the six days:

- **Young-earth (literal 24-hour days):** creation took six ordinary days a few thousand years ago; the flood explains much of the geological record. Many Baptist and Pentecostal believers hold this.
- **Day-age (old-earth):** each "day" is a long period, since the Hebrew *yom* can mean an age.
- **Framework view:** the days are a literary frame arranging God's works by topic, teaching who created rather than how long it took.

Each view seeks to honour Scripture. All reject the idea that the world came about by chance without God.

terms.def: The pattern of Genesis 1: days 1-3 form realms, days 4-6 fill them.
God's verdict on the finished creation (Genesis 1:31).
The day of rest God blessed, patterned on His rest after creation.
The view that creation took six literal days a few thousand years ago.
The view that the creation days are long periods of time.
The view that the days are a literary frame arranged by topic.

texts.teaches: God saw everything He had made, and it was very good.
Every creature of God is good, received with thanksgiving.
God ended His work on the seventh day and rested.
The sabbath was made for man.
With the Lord one day is as a thousand years.

summary: God formed and filled the world in an ordered way.
Creation, including the material world, is very good.
God's rest set a pattern of work and rest, fulfilled in rest in Christ.
Christians hold young-earth, day-age and framework views of the days, all affirming God as Creator.

questions.q: What was God's verdict on the finished creation?
Why did God rest on the seventh day?
options: To mark completion and delight in His work

questions.q: Which view reads the creation days as long periods?
What do all faithful views of Genesis 1 agree on?
options: The exact age of the earth

modules.title: God's Providence
modules.intro: God did not wind up the world and walk away. This week we learn how He preserves and governs all things.

lessons.title: Preservation
lessons.body:
Providence has three aspects. The first is **preservation**: God keeps everything in existence. Christ upholds "all things by the word of his power" (Hebrews 1:3); "by him all things consist" (hold together) (Colossians 1:17). "In him we live, and move, and have our being" (Acts 17:28).

If God withdrew His hand for a moment, creation would cease. The regular laws of nature are not independent forces; they are God's faithful way of upholding the world (Genesis 8:22; Jeremiah 33:25).

lessons.title: Concurrence and government
lessons.body:
The second aspect is **concurrence**: God works together with the things He has made, so that they act according to their nature while He directs them. Rain falls by natural laws, yet "he giveth rain upon the earth" (Job 5:10). Farmers labour, yet God gives the increase (1 Corinthians 3:7).

The third is **government**: God directs all things to His purposes. "The king's heart is in the hand of the LORD" (Proverbs 21:1). "The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole disposing thereof is of the LORD" (Proverbs 16:33).

God governs nations (Daniel 2:21), nature (Psalm 147:8) and individual lives (Psalm 139:16).

lessons.title: Providence and evil
lessons.body:
If God governs all things, what about evil? Scripture teaches that God is never the author of sin (James 1:13), and people are responsible for their wrongs. Yet God can overrule evil for good.

Joseph said to his brothers, "ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good" (Genesis 50:20). The cross is the supreme example: wicked men crucified Jesus, yet it happened by "the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God" for our salvation (Acts 2:23).

We may not understand every trial, but we know "all things work together for good to them that love God" (Romans 8:28).

terms.def: God's ongoing care and control of all things.
God's keeping of all creation in existence.
God working with created things as they act according to their nature.
God's directing of all things to His purposes.
The regular patterns by which God faithfully upholds creation.
One who causes and approves sin; God is never this.

texts.teaches: Christ upholds all things by the word of His power.
By Christ all things hold together.
The king's heart is in the hand of the LORD.
God tempts no one to evil.
God meant for good what people meant for evil.

summary: Providence has three aspects: preservation, concurrence and government.
Christ upholds all things; natural laws are His faithful working.
God governs nations, nature and individual lives.
God is not the author of sin, but He overrules evil for good.

questions.q: Which aspect of providence means God keeps all things in existence?

options: The king's heart is in the LORD's hand

questions.q: Is God the author of sin?
options: No; He tempts no one, though He overrules evil for good

questions.q: What is the supreme example of God turning evil to good?

modules.title: Living Under God's Care
modules.intro: Belief in creation and providence changes how we worship, work, pray and face fear. This week is practical.

lessons.title: Worship the Creator
lessons.body:
Creation calls us to worship. "O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the LORD our maker" (Psalm 95:6). Paul warns against those who "worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator" (Romans 1:25).

This rules out idols, charms, and trust in the stars, spirits or ancestral powers. Nothing in creation deserves the honour that belongs to God alone.

It also calls us to care for creation as stewards. God put Adam in the garden "to dress it and to keep it" (Genesis 2:15). The earth is the Lord's (Psalm 24:1), not ours to waste.

lessons.title: Freedom from fear
lessons.body:
Jesus taught His disciples not to be anxious, because the Father feeds the birds and clothes the lilies: "your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things" (Matthew 6:32). Not a sparrow falls without Him, and "the very hairs of your head are all numbered" (Matthew 10:30).

Providence frees believers from fear of witchcraft, bad luck and evil powers. "If God be for us, who can be against us?" (Romans 8:31).

It also frees us from pride in success: "it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth" (Deuteronomy 8:18).

lessons.title: Providence and prayer
lessons.body:
If God has planned all things, why pray? Because God has ordained prayer as one of the means by which He works. "Ye have not, because ye ask not" (James 4:2). Elijah prayed and the rain stopped and returned (James 5:17-18).

Providence does not make us passive. Nehemiah prayed and set a watch (Nehemiah 4:9). Paul trusted God for the ship's safety yet insisted the sailors stay aboard (Acts 27:22-31).

So we pray boldly, work diligently and leave the results to our faithful God: "Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him" (Psalm 37:5).

terms.def: Caring for what belongs to God as His managers.
Giving the honour due to God to anything created.
The ordinary ways, such as prayer and work, through which God accomplishes His purposes.
Worry about the future that providence calls us to bring to God.
The false idea that what will be will be, regardless of prayer or action.
Humanity's God-given responsibility to rule and care for the earth.

texts.teaches: Worship and kneel before the LORD our maker.
Man was placed in the garden to dress it and keep it.
Your heavenly Father knows what you need.
You have not, because you ask not.
Commit your way to the LORD and trust Him.

summary: Worship the Creator, not created things.
Care for creation as God's stewards.
Providence frees us from fear and from pride.
Pray and work diligently, for God works through means.

options: Worshipping the creature more than the Creator

questions.q: Why should believers not be anxious, according to Matthew 6?
options: The Father knows what they need
God does not care about food

questions.q: How did Paul show that trusting providence does not mean being passive?
options: He insisted the sailors stay aboard the ship
The false idea that prayer and action make no difference

short.q: Explain what creation ex nihilo means and give one Bible reference.
short.model: God created everything out of nothing by His word, as Hebrews 11:3 says: things seen were not made of things which do appear.

short.q: Why did God create the world?
short.model: For His own glory, not because He was lonely or needed anything; creation displays His perfections.

short.q: Describe two views of the days of Genesis 1 fairly.
short.model: The young-earth view reads them as six literal days; the day-age view reads each as a long period (or the framework view sees a literary arrangement). All affirm God as Creator.

short.q: Name and explain the three aspects of providence.
short.model: Preservation (God keeps all things in being), concurrence (God works with creatures as they act), and government (God directs all things to His purposes).

short.q: How can God govern all things without being the author of sin?
short.model: People are responsible for their sin and God tempts no one, yet God overrules evil for good, as with Joseph and the cross.

short.q: If God has planned everything, why should we pray?
short.model: Because God has ordained prayer as a means through which He works; He commands us to ask and answers prayer.

lists.q: List the three Persons involved in creation.
List the three aspects of providence.
List three views of the days of Genesis.

assignments.title: God in the ordinary
assignments.prompt: Describe an event in your life or community in which you now see God's providence. Using at least three passages from this course, explain how preservation, concurrence or government applies, and how it should shape your trust today.

assignments.title: Creation and our culture
assignments.prompt: Explain how belief in God as Creator answers one practice or belief common in your environment (for example trust in charms, astrology, fear of witchcraft or careless destruction of the environment). Use Scripture throughout.
